title: Best price scraping tools in 2026: we compared 13 tools on pricing and monitoring
summary: Compare 13 price scraping tools by category, pricing, and monitoring features. See how Firecrawl extracts variant-level prices and tracks product changes over time.
body_markdown:
A competitor drops a price on Friday, and you find out on Monday when your sales do. Price scraping tools close that gap by pulling prices, sale prices and stock from store pages and checking them again on a schedule. This guide compares 13 of the best price scraping tools across four kinds, then shows how to get variant-level prices and price-drop alerts with Firecrawl.


## TL;DR


- **Pick a tool that returns price, original price and stock for each size or color.** On the Allbirds page we tested, a $70 sale price applied to seven sizes, but only size 10 was in stock.
- **For supported retailers, skip scraping.** Firecrawl Alexandria returns Best Buy, Walmart and Newegg prices from providers on one Firecrawl key.
- **For every other store, Firecrawl reads the page without a schema.** The product format returns prices and stock for each size or color as JSON.
- **For bulk price data, skip the collection work.** Firecrawl Alexandria Datasets builds a custom price dataset to your schema and delivers it to your bucket, refreshed weekly or monthly.
- **A price check only pays off when it repeats.** Firecrawl /monitor re-checks pages as often as every 5 minutes, and with a goal set, it alerts you only when a price drops.
- **Other tools trade control for convenience.** No-code scrapers and monitoring platforms are quicker to start, but schedules and alerts depend on the plan. Open source libraries are free, but you maintain the selectors.


## What is price scraping?


Price scraping is the automated collection of product prices, usually with sale prices, stock and variants, so you can compare them and track them over time. Ecommerce teams, price comparison sites and builders of[product data APIs for AI shopping agents](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/product-data-api) all use it.


A price scraper visits product pages, reads the displayed or embedded product data, and turns it into fields you can store or compare. Teams use the results to follow competitors, check their own listings, and match offers across stores.


### Price scraping vs. price monitoring


Price scraping captures prices at a point in time. Price monitoring repeats those checks, compares snapshots, keeps a history, and sends notifications when a relevant change appears. Firecrawl /scrape collects a snapshot, and Firecrawl /monitor schedules recurring checks, the same way you would[monitor a website for changes](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/monitor-website-changes-firecrawl) .


Typical use cases include:


- Ecommerce price scraping to follow your own catalog across stores
- Competitor price scraping to find price or stock changes
- Price comparisons that match the same product and variant across retailers

The 13 tools fall into four kinds. Web data APIs return price fields from a URL, no-code scrapers let you click and export, monitoring platforms add matching and alerts, and open source libraries leave everything to your code.


## Web data APIs for price scraping


A web data API takes a URL and returns data, and you write the code that decides which pages to check, how often and where results go. That makes this group the best fit for developers and AI agents. Within the group, tools differ in whether they return parsed price fields or HTML you still have to parse.


### Firecrawl


Firecrawl turns any product page into structured data. The[Firecrawl /scrape](https://www.firecrawl.dev/scrape) product format reads variant prices, original prices and stock without a schema, and[Firecrawl /monitor](https://www.firecrawl.dev/monitor) re-checks them on a schedule. 67% of Fortune 100 companies use Firecrawl.


On top of its web scraping and web search APIs, Firecrawl includes[Firecrawl Alexandria](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/) , a[data connector](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/data-connectors) and[API aggregator](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/api-aggregator) that reaches data providers, including official ones such as Shopify, through one Firecrawl key. Few other web data APIs offer anything like it. For supported retailers it skips the page entirely and returns Best Buy, Walmart and Newegg prices, Shopify catalog search and StockX resale listings.


If you want the prices delivered instead,[Firecrawl Alexandria Datasets](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/datasets) builds a custom dataset to your schema and drops it in your bucket.


The Free plan includes 1,000 Firecrawl credits a month, and[Firecrawl pricing](https://www.firecrawl.dev/pricing) lists the paid plans.


Seehow to scrape prices with Firecrawl below for code and an agent prompt.


### Bright Data


Bright Data sells ready-made scrapers and datasets, billed per record. Each retailer has its own scraper, so check that the one you pick returns variant and sale-price fields before you build on it.


### Oxylabs


Oxylabs' Web API is built for collection at scale, with a scheduler for repeat jobs. Depending on the target, it returns parsed JSON or raw HTML, so for many stores you still write and maintain the parsing that turns a page into a price.


### ScrapingBee


ScrapingBee renders pages and extracts fields with rules or AI queries from your code. It doesn't include scheduling or price alerts, so repeat checks and change detection need a separate workflow.


### Apify


Apify offers ready-made scrapers, called Actors, for many retailers, plus scheduling. Each Actor is built and maintained on its own, so fields, upkeep and any Actor-specific charges vary from store to store.


## No-code price scrapers


No-code scrapers trade flexibility for speed. You click the price on a page, and the tool learns where to find it. For price work, schedules, API access and alerts usually sit on paid plans, and a click-trained scraper can return empty values when a store redesigns its page.


### Octoparse


Octoparse has templates and a point-and-click builder for people who don't code. Scheduled cloud runs and API access start on the Standard plan, so the lower plans can't re-check prices unattended.


### Browse AI


Browse AI trains a robot on the columns you click and can monitor pages for changes. How often it can check depends on your plan, so confirm that interval matches how fast prices move in your market.


### Web Scraper


Web Scraper is a free Chrome extension that exports CSV or XLSX. Unattended, scheduled runs need a paid Cloud plan, and the extension alone has no alerts.


## Price monitoring platforms


Price monitoring platforms are price scraping software built for pricing teams. They add product matching, price history and alerts on top of the scraping. You get answers in a dashboard rather than raw data, and plans are sized by how many products and competitors you track.


### Prisync


Prisync tracks known competitor product pages and reports price and stock changes three times a day. Plans cap the number of products, and results come as a dashboard and Excel reports rather than data that flows into your own systems.


### Price2Spy


Price2Spy covers monitoring, comparisons and repricing. Its entry tier alerts daily, faster alerts cost more, and plan prices are quoted on request.


### Pricefy


Pricefy adds AI product matching and repricing. The free plan covers 50 SKUs with daily updates, but alerts start on Starter and repricing on Pro.


## Open source libraries for building your own price scraper


Open source libraries cost nothing, and you build every part of the job yourself, from the selectors for each store to the servers, schedule, storage and alerts.


### Scrapy


Scrapy is a free Python framework for crawling and extraction. You own the selectors, scheduling and alerts, and prices that load with JavaScript need extra rendering.


### Playwright


Playwright drives real browsers, so it reads prices that appear after JavaScript runs. It has no product schema, price history or alerts, so every store needs its own selectors.


## How to choose a price scraping tool


Test the same three pages with every shortlisted tool: one simple product page, one with sizes and a sale price, and one where the price appears after JavaScript loads. Then compare each tool's extracted fields against the page.


### Does it read prices that load with JavaScript?


Try a page where the visible price appears after the initial HTML loads, the case[tools for scraping pages that load with JavaScript](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/dynamic-scraping-tools) are built for. Compare the extracted price to the rendered page. A successful HTTP response with an empty price is still a failed price check.


### Does it return price fields or raw HTML?


Look for product identifiers, current price, original price, currency and variant-level availability. If the tool returns HTML, budget time to write and maintain the parsing logic. If it returns JSON, verify each field against the page.


### What happens when a store changes its page layout?


Re-check after selecting a different size or color, or try a similar page with a different template. Record missing fields as errors rather than treating them as zero prices or out-of-stock products.


### Can it re-check prices on a schedule and alert you?


Test a scheduled check and verify the notification arrives. Firecrawl supports recurring monitors with email and webhook delivery; Browse AI and pricing platforms also offer scheduled workflows. Distinguish an initial “new page” event from a later changed-price notification.


### What will each price cost at your volume?


Vendors charge by credits, records, tasks, monitored products or checked URLs. Estimate checks per day, number of URLs and any extraction add-ons, then compare totals over the same time period.[Firecrawl pricing](https://www.firecrawl.dev/pricing) lists Firecrawl's plans and the Firecrawl credits each one includes per month.


## How to scrape prices with Firecrawl


Check Firecrawl Alexandria first. For[Best Buy](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/bestbuy-com) ,[Walmart](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/walmart-com) ,[Newegg](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/newegg-com) ,[Shopify](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/shopify) stores and[StockX](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/stockx-com) , it returns prices from providers on one Firecrawl key, so nothing has to load a page and a layout change can't break it. For every other store, the steps after it work on any product page.


The Python examples and agent prompt below run on brand product pages. The values were captured on November 10, 2026, and live prices and availability change.


### Check retailer prices with Firecrawl Alexandria


Finding a tool in[Firecrawl Alexandria](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/) is free, and running one is charged at its listed price. These[retail providers](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/categories/retail) cover the price jobs in this post:

For StockX,` products/search_products` finds product candidates; use a follow-up product lookup for more detailed market data. The Shopify catalog search is also for discovery, and its results don't show a store's full stock.


Use Firecrawl Alexandria when a provider supports the retailer and fields you need, and the Firecrawl /scrape product format below for any other store. To see both together, the[Black Friday price tracker](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/black-friday-price-tracker) pulls Shopify, Walmart and Best Buy prices through Firecrawl Alexandria and watches sale pages with Firecrawl /monitor.


To try it, ask in plain English from ChatGPT or Claude:


```text
Use Firecrawl Alexandria to find the current Walmart price
for the Sony WH-1000XM5 headphones.
```

### Read a product page with the Firecrawl /scrape product format


The[Firecrawl /scrape product format](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/scrape#extract-product-data) reads merchant product data without a custom schema or LLM extraction step. You can also try the[free product data extractor](https://www.firecrawl.dev/tools/product-data-extractor) without writing code.


The product object has these parts:


- Title, brand, category, URL and description.
- Variants, each with an ID, SKU, title and option values.
- Per variant: price with currency, original price and availability.


Install the Python SDK with` pip install firecrawl-py` , then run:


```text
from   firecrawl   import   Firecrawl


firecrawl   =   Firecrawl  (api_key  =  "fc-YOUR-API-KEY"  )


result   =   firecrawl  .  scrape  (
"https://www.allbirds.com/products/mens-tree-runners-navy-night"  ,
formats  =  [  "product"  ],
)
print  (result.product.  model_dump_json  (indent  =  2  , by_alias  =  True  , exclude_none  =  True  ))
```


Replace` fc-YOUR-API-KEY` with your own key. As of November 2026, the page showed a price of 70 USD with an original price of 100 USD, and only size 10 was in stock. The response listed seven size variants. This trimmed output removes image lists and some fields, and changes no value:


```text
{
"title"  :   "Men's Tree Runner - Navy Night (White Sole)"  ,
"brand"  :   "Allbirds"  ,
"variants"  :   [
{
"sku"  :   "TR3MNNW100"  ,
"title"  :   "10"  ,
"values"  :   {   "size"  :   "10"   }  ,
"price"  :   {   "amount"  :   70  ,   "currency"  :   "USD"   }  ,
"sale"  :   {   "originalPrice"  :   {   "amount"  :   100  ,   "currency"  :   "USD"   } }  ,
"availability"  :   {   "inStock"  :   true   }
}
]
}
```


The six other sizes in the full response were marked out of stock, so a product-level price only means something next to each variant's availability.


The free extractor shows the same page's data. It reports 7 variants, 70 USD, sale pricing detected, 1 in stock and 6 out of stock, and its Preview and Product JSON tabs show the same product.


### Pull other fields with JSON mode


JSON mode takes a schema inside the format object. We asked for three fields with the Firecrawl Python SDK:


```text
from   firecrawl   import   Firecrawl
from   pydantic   import   BaseModel


class   Offer  (  BaseModel  ):
price  :   str
shipping_offer  :   str
promo_text  :   str


result   =   Firecrawl  (api_key  =  "fc-YOUR-API-KEY"  ).  scrape  (
"https://www.allbirds.com/products/mens-tree-runners-navy-night"  ,
formats  =  [{  "type"  :   "json"  ,   "schema"  : Offer.  model_json_schema  ()}],
)
print  (result.json)
```


A fresh JSON-mode check returned these fields:


```text
{
"price"  :   "$70"  ,
"shipping_offer"  :   "Free ground shipping on orders over $100"  ,
"promo_text"  :   "Black Friday Early Access. Up to 70% off select styles."
}
```


The shipping text is a conditional offer with no numeric cost, so the schema asks for` shipping_offer` instead of` shipping_cost` .


Keep the schema narrow with only the fields you need, and spot-check results against the page before saving them. For variant prices and stock, the product format above is the better fit.

### Get alerts when a price changes with Firecrawl /monitor


A[Firecrawl monitor](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/monitoring) re-checks pages on a schedule, with a minimum interval of 5 minutes. JSON change tracking compares fields such as price and availability. This is the daily, three-page monitor we ran:


```text
import   os
from   firecrawl   import   Firecrawl


urls   =   [
"https://www.allbirds.com/products/mens-tree-runners-navy-night"  ,
"https://www.brooklinen.com/products/classic-core-sheet-set"  ,
"https://bombas.com/products/men-s-solid-ankle-sock-white-large-1"  ,
]
price_schema   =   {
"type"  :   "object"  ,
"properties"  :   {
"price"  :   {  "type"  :   "string"  },
"availability"  :   {  "type"  :   "string"  },
},
}


monitor   =   Firecrawl  (api_key  =  os.environ[  "FIRECRAWL_API_KEY"  ]).  create_monitor  (
name  =  "Price and stock monitor"  ,
schedule  =  {  "text"  :   "daily"  ,   "timezone"  :   "UTC"  },
targets  =  [{
"type"  :   "scrape"  ,   "urls"  : urls,
"scrapeOptions"  : {  "formats"  : [{
"type"  :   "changeTracking"  ,   "modes"  : [  "json"  ],   "schema"  : price_schema
}]},
}],
notification  =  {  "email"  : {
"enabled"  :   True  ,   "recipients"  : [os.environ[  "ALERT_EMAIL"  ]],
"includeDiffs"  :   True  ,
}},
)
print  (monitor.id)
```


Set` FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` and` ALERT_EMAIL` as environment variables before running it. The first check records each page as new, so the email below lists 3 new pages. Later checks report changed fields, and a` goal` such as "alert me when a price drops" limits alerts to the changes you care about. The[competitor monitoring guide](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/competitor-monitoring-firecrawl) covers notifications in more depth.

Then give your agent this prompt, replacing “these 3 product pages” with your URLs:


```text

that emails me when any price drops.
```


The agent sets the price drop as the monitor's goal, so the email arrives only when a price goes down.


### Get a price dataset delivered with Firecrawl Alexandria Datasets


If you would rather receive price data than run the checks yourself,[Firecrawl Alexandria Datasets](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/datasets) builds a custom dataset to your schema. Send a list of store domains or product URLs, the fields each record needs, such as price, original price and stock per variant, and how often it should refresh.


Our data team sends a sample of about 1,000 rows first. After you approve it, the full set arrives as Parquet, JSONL or CSV, by download link or in your S3, GCS or R2 bucket, with weekly or monthly refreshes. Every record keeps the URL it came from.


## Common problems when scraping prices


Four issues often send price comparisons wrong: selecting the wrong variant, mixing currencies, matching different products, and missing page changes.


### Variants and sale prices


A crossed-out original price is the old price, and only the displayed sale price is current. Store the displayed sale price, original price, stock status, and variant identifier separately. Firecrawl's product format exposes these as variant-level fields when the page supplies them. Verify a discounted offer against the specific size or color a shopper can buy.


### Currency and regional prices


Store prices with the currency and region displayed on the page. A` $70` result does not establish which country or shipping destination applies. Firecrawl's product format reports a currency only when it finds one in the source, including[schema.org Product](https://schema.org/Product) data. Avoid guessing a currency when the field is absent.


### Matching the same product across stores


Matching the wrong size, pack quantity or bundle can make accurate prices look inconsistent. Start with a confirmed SKU or[GTIN](https://www.gs1.org/standards/id-keys/gtin) , then confirm the exact variant and unit quantity before comparing. Firecrawl Alexandria's[Affiliate.com URL-to-barcode tool](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers/affiliate-com) can help identify a product across retailers, but matching still needs validation.


### When a store changes its layout


A layout change can leave a selector-based scraper returning an empty value. Treat missing prices as extraction errors, log the affected URLs, and inspect a sample after template changes. Firecrawl's product format does not require custom selectors. When it cannot identify a product confidently, its documented behavior is to omit the product object and return a warning rather than guess.


Storefront variety is the norm, as[Minimal's Firecrawl customer story](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/how-minimal-builds-ai-support-agents-with-firecrawl) shows:


> Storefronts come to us in every shape imaginable, and no matter the complexity, Firecrawl turns each one into clean, structured data our AI support agents can answer from.


—[Niek Hogenboom](https://www.linkedin.com/in/niek-hogenboom/) , Co-Founder at[Minimal](https://gominimal.ai/)


## Why is a price data aggregator better than a single provider?


On top of its web scraping API, which reads any store's product page into price, original price and stock fields, Firecrawl offers Firecrawl Alexandria as a price data aggregator. A price data aggregator puts several retailer data sources behind one API, so one integration reaches catalogs and prices that no single store publishes for its rivals. Through Firecrawl Alexandria, Best Buy, Walmart, Newegg, Shopify, StockX and Affiliate.com sit on the same Firecrawl key as the scraping API, each returning JSON from the same call.


Firecrawl has more than 200,000 stars on[GitHub](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl) . In the evaluation published with the[Firecrawl Alexandria launch](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/introducing-alexandria-series-b) , AI agents using Firecrawl Alexandria scored 21% higher on answer quality than agents using built-in web tools, across 845 tasks with the same model and prompts and blind AI judging.


- **More of the market covered.** Best Buy and Newegg return product prices, Shopify searches across many stores, and StockX lists resale offers. A comparison that spans those retailers reaches each one through the same key.
- **One integration to maintain.** The tools above bill by records, API credits, tasks or monitored products, and each needs its own account. Through Firecrawl Alexandria you keep one client, one response format and one Firecrawl credit balance.
- **A fallback when a provider can't answer.** Best Buy, Walmart and Newegg all answer catalog searches, so a search can move to another retailer when one comes back empty, and the Firecrawl /scrape product format reads any store no provider covers.
- **Pay per call, with no lock-in.** Each run is charged at its listed price, so adding Affiliate.com barcode matching later means one more call on the same key, with no new vendor account.


## Which price scraping tool should you pick?


Pick a price scraping tool by who runs it and what it has to return.


- **Developers and AI agents** should start with Firecrawl, because the product format returns variant prices and stock as fields and Firecrawl /monitor re-checks them on a schedule.
- **Pricing teams** get product matching and alerts built in with Prisync, Price2Spy or Pricefy.
- **Teams that want bulk price data** without running scrapers can request a custom dataset from Firecrawl Alexandria Datasets.
- **People who don't code** can ask Firecrawl Alexandria in ChatGPT or Claude for a Best Buy or Walmart price in plain English, with no scraper to set up. For other stores, Octoparse, Browse AI or Web Scraper let you click the price you want and export it.
- **Engineers who want full control** can build on Scrapy or Playwright.

Pricing team tracking competitors Prisync, Price2Spy, Pricefy Start a free trial and check the product and alert limits of each plan

Whichever kind you choose, test it on your own pages first. If you want to go further with Firecrawl, you can[build a price tracker in Python](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/automated-price-tracking-tutorial-python) or set up a[competitor price monitoring system](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/automated-competitor-price-scraping) .
